In the video game community people generally seem to be against piracy (except if there is restrictive DRM).

People who are into music seem to be against it too.

With movies, and books the general feeling is that no one cares.

I get movies, where some feel that it's fine because studios are making lots of money, but what about books, and writers? Out of everyone writers make the least amount of money. A book can take anywhere from one to two years to produce, and writers typically make 8.5% or less of the cover price. With self publishing the biggest player on the market, Amazon, takes 70% of your sales, and gives your books away for free too.

According to an article, which I think is mostly true, the average writer makes less than £600 a year. That's not even minimum wage. When I wrote a book I gave it out for free. It took me around 6 or 7 months of full time work to write. Over 10,000 people downloaded it, and gave it 4/5 stars. I added a saleslink, and only got $27.00 in return.

But this isn't about my personal failings...!

My question is: What is it about books that makes people more inclined towards piracy, or feel less guilty about it? What is the distinction that makes it okay to pirate a book, but not a video game, or a music album? Or am I wrong about it? Is there less piracy for books percentage-wise?
When it comes to piracy why is it that certain communities are against it, while others are not?

That's a good question. Something I myself am on the fence about. Being a capitalist, I know that having copyright laws stimulate creation because it allows people to profit from their produced works. However, people have also been very successful collecting money less directly, in ways I consider to be a form of 'busking.'

I think why most people support piracy is because the copyright laws are very strict and last far too long. They also tend to disproportionally affect the 'little guy' because it is possible to skirt copyright laws with minor tweaks, but be expected to discuss it in court.

Short and less than all inclusive response, but perhaps it get the ball rolling.

My main issue with copyright law is:

a) How it is enforced.

b) How derivative works are treated.

For example, spying on people to enforce copyright is wrong, and also taking them to court, and trying to extract an insane amount of cash from them. I think that's not only stupid, but immoral too. I also dislike it when companies legally threaten individuals who make art that is inspired from elsewhere, or they shut them down because they've innocently borrowed something of theirs. That is overstepping the boundaries of copyright. I read a story once where Disney forced a daycare to remove their mural because it contained Disney characters. Which I think is a really, really shitty thing to do. Then of recent you Nintendo, which has been going around flagging "Let's Play" videos for recording Super Mario characters. It makes no sense really, since a video is like free advertising, but that goes to show how copyright laws should be updated.

However, I still find it strange how people justify piracy. If you're going to pirate just say: "I don't want to pay for that, because I'm broke, or I'm a little greedy." Why give all these weird explanations? It's clear what the motivation is. A commenter below for example just said s/he will not pay for something if it's not in a physical format. I found that to be really bizarre. Dishonesty cannot be justified in such a way... Can it? S/he said he is gainfully employed, so I have some qualms with that, pirating just because it's not physically available. You are still enjoying someone's work, and they won't be able to make a living because you've given that justification for piracy.
